THE HEADLINE FINDING. Running the key-FORM check across EVERY hub, as instructed, finds the same defect class UNFIXED on HUB_DOCUMENT: DOCUMENT_ID is keyed 'DOC:'-prefixed on 2 quote-branch rows and bare on 20 document-detail rows. One document identifier, two hub rows. It was present at the baseline too - the fix addressed the two instances the mapper had found, not the class. Under the three repair rules the map goes 3 findings -> 1, and the survivor is real. Proposed default: build the bare form on all 22 as a recorded builder decision.

The ORG_UNIT fix left the inverse risk in place. BRANCH_CODE (4 rows), LOCATION_CODE (1) and STORED_COMPANY_CODE (1) all key HUB_ORG_UNIT with NO prefix, so equal values from three different code systems merge into one hub row. By the mapper's own rule (splitting is recoverable, merging is not) the unprefixed state is the unsafe direction. Proposed default: prefix each with its own namespace ('BRANCH:', 'LOC:', 'COMPANY:') and declare it.

As asked: 'ORGHUB:' || nullif(trim(HUB_LOCATION),'') keys HUB_ORG_UNIT on a source column literally named HUB_LOCATION, on one row of ..._CLAIM_ATTRIBUTE_PROPERTIES_PIVOT_VW, under a prefix used nowhere else in the map. Either the column is a mis-named org code or an org unit is being keyed on a location. CONFIRMED still distinct - the fix did not merge it. Build as written and flag; merging would be unrecoverable.

The ORG_UNIT fix put an md5 of a branch NAME into the same 'ORGUNIT:' namespace as office CODES. They cannot collide textually so no rows merge wrongly, but one physical branch still produces two hub rows and the shared prefix now hides that. This form also uses md5(upper(trim(...))), the SECOND canonicalisation, not md5(normalise(...)).

Hub key vs LINK LEG byte-identity, swept across every hub and link as instructed: 16 disagreements, 9 whitespace-only and 7 VALUE-CHANGING. Identical at the baseline, so pre-existing. The two that matter: (a) HUB_CLAIM on CLAIM_RESERVE - the hub key walks on FOREIGN_KEY and the leg on PARENT_KEY_HASH, so the link depends on the UNPROVEN FK round-trip; (b) an ORPHAN leg 'EMP:' || BAGIC_RM_ECODE on two pivots, where no HUB_PARTY key anywhere is built from BAGIC_RM_ECODE - the only 'EMP:' hub keys use BAGIC_EMPLOYEE_CODE. Stage 2 must emit the hub key expression for every leg by construction so the two cannot diverge.

51 of the 91 LNK legs are POSITIONAL and name no hub, so the leg-equals-hub-key property cannot be checked from the map alone. More than half the link surface is unverified for the property that silently produces empty joins. Stage 2 must resolve positional legs against the link definition in data_7.js and assert the property there; if a leg order cannot be resolved, do not build that link.
